nodes.label: SubZeroDev.WinGet (library overview)
nodes.rationale: Wraps the WinGet COM API so callers avoid CsWinRT projections, COM activation quirks in elevated hosts, AND-only search filters, and WinRT structs; chosen over shelling out to winget.exe because column-aligned console tables are fragile against column widths, truncation ellipses, and non-Latin characters.

nodes.label: WinGet COM API (Microsoft.Management.Deployment)
nodes.rationale: The same in-process API winget.exe itself is built on; gives structured, typed access to the same engine instead of parsed console output.

nodes.label: No COM/WinRT types in the public surface
nodes.rationale: Callers only ever see plain C# records, enums, and interfaces, so COM/WinRT interop details never leak into consuming code.
nodes.norm_label: no com/winrt types in the public surface

nodes.label: No Async method-name suffix convention
nodes.rationale: Every operation returns a Task, so the Async suffix would carry no information and is treated as noise.

nodes.label: The one deliberate CLI exception
nodes.rationale: Pin management and export/import have no COM equivalent at any WinGet contract version (verified against the winget-cli IDL), so only those two features shell out to winget.exe, isolated behind IWinGetCliClient; everything else stays pure COM.

nodes.label: Service layer
nodes.rationale: What most consumers should use: adds input validation, structured logging via ILogger<T>, result normalization, and the documented auto-retry policy on top of the client layer.

nodes.label: Client layer
nodes.rationale: Thin, single-attempt translations to/from the COM API (or CLI for the two COM-gap features), exposed so callers who want full control over retry behavior can bypass the service layer.

nodes.label: Activation layer
nodes.rationale: Internal layer that creates every COM object through one resilient activation chain so all COM objects share a single activation context.

nodes.label: IWinGetCliClient
nodes.rationale: Isolates the only two CLI-backed features (pins, export/import) behind one interface so the winget.exe dependency cannot spread into the rest of the library.

nodes.label: Resilient COM activation chain
nodes.rationale: Three ordered modes — WinRT projection activation (new PackageManager()), CoCreateInstance with CLSCTX_LOCAL_SERVER against winget-cli's out-of-proc production CLSIDs, then CoCreateInstance with CLSCTX_ALLOW_LOWER_TRUST_REGISTRATION (the documented mitigation for elevated hosts, as used by the WinGet PowerShell module and UniGetUI). The first success is cached so every COM object shares one activation context; if all three fail, WinGetUnavailableException is thrown.

nodes.label: Composite catalogs everywhere
nodes.rationale: Every lookup merges remote sources with local install state via CreateCompositePackageCatalog, the architecturally correct approach and what winget itself does, so installed state correlates with available versions; get-by-id and mutating operations need the exact CatalogPackage WinGet associates with the installed app for upgrade/uninstall/repair to work at all.

nodes.label: Unreachable-source resilience
nodes.rationale: If the composite catalog fails to connect, each source is probed individually and the composite is rebuilt from the reachable subset rather than failing the whole call.

nodes.label: Selectors are OR'd, Filters are AND'd
nodes.rationale: Verified by running the API: FindPackagesOptions.Selectors are OR'd while Filters are AND'd, so multi-field search (name or id or moniker or tag) is a single call carrying multiple Selectors.
nodes.norm_label: selectors are or'd, filters are and'd

nodes.label: Indexed for-loops over CsWinRT collections
nodes.rationale: Enumerating a CsWinRT-projected IReadOnlyList<T> via foreach/LINQ throws InvalidCastException in interop 1.29.280, so all collection traversal uses indexed for loops and must not be 'simplified'.

nodes.label: ExtendedErrorCode is an Exception, not an int
nodes.rationale: InstallResult.ExtendedErrorCode is typed as an Exception, so the HRESULT must be read from its .HResult property.
nodes.norm_label: extendederrorcode is an exception, not an int

nodes.label: Separate progress mappers per operation
nodes.rationale: InstallProgress and UninstallProgress are different WinRT structs with public fields, so a single shared mapper is impossible.

nodes.label: WinGetUnavailableException
nodes.rationale: A typed exception so a raw COMException never escapes when WinGet is missing, too old, or COM activation is blocked.

nodes.label: WinGetErrorCodes
nodes.rationale: Exposes well-known APPINSTALLER_CLI_ERROR_* HRESULTs already unchecked-cast to int so they compare directly against ExtendedErrorCode.

nodes.label: Hosting caveats (elevation, SYSTEM, concurrency)
nodes.rationale: COM activation under LocalSystem and winget's scope behavior in profile-less contexts are not yet validated by the test suite, so service hosting is an open item; the library also adds no global lock because WinGet already serializes some source operations internally.

nodes.label: AddPackageManagement()
nodes.rationale: Registers the full public surface (both services and all three clients) as singletons in one call.

nodes.label: The one integration rule (direct ComInterop reference)
nodes.rationale: The Microsoft.WindowsPackageManager.ComInterop build targets copy the native Microsoft.Management.Deployment.dll only into the output of projects that reference the package directly; it does not flow transitively, so any project that runs library code needs its own PackageReference or the first COM call fails with COMException 0x80040154 (REGDB_E_CLASSNOTREG).
nodes.norm_label: the one integration rule (direct cominterop reference)

nodes.label: x64 platform pinning requirement
nodes.rationale: The WinGet interop assembly is not AnyCPU, so consuming projects must pin Platform/PlatformTarget to x64; ARM64 is declared but not yet validated on hardware.

nodes.label: GitHub Packages NuGet feed
nodes.rationale: GitHub requires authentication even for a public packages feed, so consumers must supply a PAT with read:packages as the source password.

nodes.label: Error handling model (throw vs result)
nodes.rationale: Only environmental unavailability throws (typed WinGetUnavailableException); operation failures such as a failed install or a package not found return a result record with Succeeded, a normalized Status, the ExtendedErrorCode HRESULT, and the installer's own exit code.

nodes.label: SubZeroDev.WinGet.Examples console project
nodes.rationale: Holds a runnable example for every public API and doubles as the working reference for the direct ComInterop package reference, DI composition, progress reporting, Ctrl+C cancellation, and typed unavailability handling.

nodes.label: Read-only examples
nodes.rationale: Run live against the machine's WinGet but change nothing, so they are safe to run without arguments.

nodes.label: Mutating examples
nodes.rationale: Because they change the machine, they require explicit arguments and print usage then exit when run bare — a deliberate guard against accidental mutation.

nodes.label: Nuke build orchestration
nodes.rationale: A thin generic layer over the same dotnet commands so CI calls targets instead of hand-written steps; build/_build.csproj targets net10.0 because Nuke.Common 10.x ships lib/net10.0 only, while the product stays on net8, and the build.ps1/build.sh bootstrappers are required because the Nuke global tool locates a build by searching for them.

nodes.label: Mocked unit test suite
nodes.rationale: 100 tests with zero COM dependency so they run anywhere in ~200ms, covering the service layer, CLI argument-building contracts, winget pin list parsing variants, model defaults, DI registration, and the exception type.

nodes.label: Live integration tests
nodes.rationale: 12 NUnit [Explicit] tests excluded from plain dotnet test; deliberately read-only because they run against whatever machine executes them, with mutating coverage tracked pending a disposable side-effect-free test package.

nodes.label: Coverage reporting (coverlet + ReportGenerator)
nodes.rationale: Unit-only 27.7% line vs 54% merged with a live integration run; the uncovered remainder is COM-operation internals that only execute during real mutating operations. Method coverage is not quoted because ReportGenerator 5.5.x gates that metric behind sponsorship.

nodes.label: GitHub Actions build workflow
nodes.rationale: Two jobs on windows-latest: build runs on every push to main and every PR as the required status check (single `nuke Test Coverage` invocation so the shared Restore/Compile/Test chain runs once, since Nuke only de-duplicates within one invocation), and release (needs: build) does all packing/publishing. Both check out full history, but only release truly needs it for [GitVersion]; build uses fetch-depth 0 solely to silence Nuke's eager-injection warning.

nodes.label: GitVersion versioning
nodes.rationale: Derives the version from git history rather than the .csproj <Version>; GitVersion.yml's next-version sets the base because without it GitVersion inferred 0.0.1. Per-branch deployment-mode overrides made no difference — an untagged commit is always a prerelease, which is why a stable release requires a v* tag.

nodes.label: PublishGitHubPackages target
nodes.rationale: Automatic: a push to main publishes a distinct prerelease, a v* tag publishes stable. Uses the automatic GITHUB_TOKEN so no secret is needed, and --skip-duplicate makes re-pushing an existing version harmless. The workflow's push trigger must include tags: ['v*'], because with only branches: declared GitHub never runs the workflow for tag pushes and the tag would silently publish nothing.

nodes.label: PublishNuGet target (manual)
nodes.rationale: Off by default; runs only on a manual workflow_dispatch with push_to_nuget checked and a NUGET_API_KEY secret, and publishes the .csproj-pinned version rather than the GitVersion one.

nodes.label: Running CI locally with act
nodes.rationale: Host mode is required because the job targets Windows, and it reuses the real environment so the installed Nuke global tool persists between runs; the workflow uses dotnet tool update, which is idempotent, so repeat act runs don't fail.

nodes.label: COMException 0x80040154 (REGDB_E_CLASSNOTREG)
nodes.rationale: The most common integration failure: the executable project is missing the direct ComInterop PackageReference, so the native activation DLL was never copied to its output directory.

nodes.label: WinGetUnavailableException causes
nodes.rationale: Ordered by likelihood: WinGet/App Installer not installed, WinGet too old for the pinned 1.29.x interop contract, or COM activation blocked in the process context after the lower-trust fallback already failed.

nodes.label: InvalidCastException while enumerating
nodes.rationale: Caused by converting an indexed for loop over a CsWinRT-projected collection into foreach/LINQ; only indexer access (.Count / [i]) works in interop 1.29.280. Library loops carry fence comments, and IWinGetClient results are safe because they are plain List<T> copies.

nodes.label: 0x8A150056 installer prohibits elevation
nodes.rationale: Resolve by running the process non-elevated for that package, or by checking ElevationRequirement from package details before deciding how to launch.

nodes.label: 0x8A150019 command requires admin
nodes.rationale: A machine-scope installer needs elevation the process lacks; either elevate or request PackageScope.User where supported.

nodes.label: AccessDenied adding/removing sources
nodes.rationale: Source add/remove modify machine-wide state and require an elevated caller; this is WinGet behavior, not the library's.

nodes.label: ARP\ ids in the installed catalog
nodes.rationale: Not an error: the installed catalog includes software installed outside WinGet keyed by its raw Apps-and-Features registry entry. Such entries cannot be targeted by id for install/upgrade, so update UIs should filter on the ARP\ prefix.
nodes.norm_label: arp\ ids in the installed catalog

nodes.label: Export exits non-zero but the file exists
nodes.rationale: winget export exits non-zero when some installed applications aren't available in any configured source, yet still writes the file for everything it could map, so 'file written' is the practical success signal.
nodes.norm_label: export exits non-zero but the file exists

nodes.label: Running under SYSTEM / as a Windows Service
nodes.rationale: Two caveats inherited from WinGet itself: no App Execution Alias exists in service contexts (the CLI shim already falls back to the WindowsApps package directory), and install-scope preference in profile-less contexts can behave unexpectedly — enterprise deployments patch winget's own settings.json to default to machine scope. This path is not covered by the test suite.
nodes.norm_label: running under system / as a windows service

nodes.label: Search
nodes.rationale: One call searches name, id, moniker, and tag across every configured source, with installed state already correlated into each result so no second list-installed call is needed; an optional sourceName restricts it to one source.

nodes.label: GetInstalled
nodes.rationale: Returns non-WinGet software with a raw ARP registry key as its Id, which cannot be targeted for install/upgrade — check the ARP\ prefix before offering an Update button.

nodes.label: GetAvailableUpgrades
nodes.rationale: The winget upgrade equivalent.

nodes.label: GetPackage
nodes.rationale: Returns null when the package is not found rather than throwing.

nodes.label: GetDetails
nodes.rationale: Returns the full catalog manifest: description, publisher URLs, license, copyright, release notes, agreements, documentation links, icons, tags, and every available version.

nodes.label: Install
nodes.rationale: An empty or null InstallRequest reproduces a plain `winget install <id>`, so callers opt into option control rather than being forced to supply it.

nodes.label: InstallRequest
nodes.rationale: Carries Version (null means latest applicable), Scope, Mode, Architecture, InstallerType, PreferredInstallLocation, OverrideArguments (replaces installer args, --override), AdditionalArguments (appended, --custom), and AcceptPackageAgreements.

nodes.label: Update
nodes.rationale: Takes the same InstallRequest as Install so option handling stays uniform.

nodes.label: Download
nodes.rationale: The winget download equivalent: fetches the installer without running it.

nodes.label: Repair
nodes.rationale: The winget repair equivalent; requires the package's installer technology to support repair.

nodes.label: PackageOperationResult
nodes.rationale: Carries Succeeded, a normalized Status enum, ErrorMessage, the WinGet ExtendedErrorCode HRESULT, the native InstallerErrorCode when the failure came from the installer, and RebootRequired.

nodes.label: Built-in auto-retry policy
nodes.rationale: Three documented rules on IPackageManagementService: already-installed / not-newer HRESULTs normalize to success; no-applicable-installer under requested architecture/installer-type/scope constraints retries once without the constraints; unknown installed version during upgrade retries once with AllowUpgradeToUnknownVersion. Callers who want none of it use IWinGetClient directly for a single unnormalized attempt.

nodes.label: Cancellation support
nodes.rationale: Every method accepts an optional CancellationToken, and in-flight installs and downloads honor cancellation.

nodes.label: Pin
nodes.rationale: Supports three pin kinds: Pinning (excluded from bulk upgrade-all, explicit upgrade still allowed), Gating (only upgrades matching a version pattern such as 2.44.*), and Blocking (no upgrade until the pin is removed).

nodes.label: GetPins
nodes.rationale: CLI-backed; its results come from parsing `winget pin list` output because no COM equivalent exists.

nodes.label: Export
nodes.rationale: Snapshots installed packages to a winget import-compatible JSON file; a non-zero exit still writes the file for everything it could map, so existence of the file is the practical success check.

nodes.label: Import
nodes.rationale: Installs everything an exported file lists, with ignoreUnavailable to skip packages no longer in any source and ignoreVersions to choose whether exported versions are honored.

nodes.label: CliOperationResult
nodes.rationale: Because there is no structured COM result for CLI-backed operations, it captures the process outcome directly: Succeeded (ExitCode == 0), ExitCode/ExitCodeHex whose hex form matches WinGet's documented APPINSTALLER_CLI_ERROR_* HRESULTs, and captured stdout/stderr.

nodes.label: winget.exe resolution strategy
nodes.rationale: Resolves the per-user App Execution Alias first, then globs the WindowsApps package directory and picks the highest version — the strategy enterprise deployments such as Winget-AutoUpdate use, which matters because service/SYSTEM contexts have no App Execution Alias. If neither works, WinGetUnavailableException is thrown.

nodes.label: GetSources
nodes.rationale: Exposes Name, Argument, Type, TrustLevel, and Priority per source, read via COM rather than CLI parsing.

nodes.label: GetSource
nodes.rationale: Returns null when the named source is not configured.

nodes.label: AddSource
nodes.rationale: Requires an elevated caller because adding a source changes machine-wide state; WinGet returns AccessDenied otherwise.

nodes.label: AddPackageSourceRequest
nodes.rationale: Carries name and URI plus Type (Microsoft.PreIndexed.Package or Microsoft.Rest), TrustLevel, IsExplicit (true hides the source unless named explicitly), and Priority.

nodes.label: RemoveSource
nodes.rationale: preserveData:false mirrors `winget source remove` (registration and data removed); preserveData:true mirrors `winget source reset` (registration removed, data kept).

nodes.label: RefreshSource
nodes.rationale: Forces the source's catalog data to update immediately.

nodes.label: UpdateSource
nodes.rationale: Changes the Explicit flag and/or Priority (higher priority sorts first); at least one must be provided or ArgumentException is thrown.

nodes.label: SourceOperationResult
nodes.rationale: Carries Succeeded, ErrorMessage, and the WinGet ExtendedErrorCode HRESULT.

nodes.label: Percentage progress for source operations
nodes.rationale: Source operations report a simple 0-100 percentage (IProgress<double>) rather than the staged progress packages use, because sources have no install/download stages to report.
